name: Porcine/Wild Boar Mandible
description:
High-resolution 3D anatomical scan of a Porcine / Wild Boar Mandible (Sus scrofa).

This digital model delivers a  representation of the lower jaw osteology in suids. The mandible showcases a robust, elongated horizontal ramus (corpus mandibulae) fused at the mental symphysis, built to withstand the heavy mechanical stress of rooting and crushing food. The scan highlights the specialized omnivorous dentition, featuring strong incisors, highly developed canine teeth (tusks, which are continuously growing and self-sharpening in wild specimens/males), and broad bunodont molars adapted for grinding varied organic matter.

Source / Provenance: This specimen is part of the anatomical collection curated by Professor Antonio Palladino, Professor of Veterinary Anatomy, Histology, and Embryology at the University of Rome Tor Vergata.

Suggested Use: Educational purposes, veterinary research, comparative anatomy study, and scientific visualization.
